$comment: Machine-readable SpotifyCares codebook. PROPOSED, not locked. Prose definitions, examples and boundary rules live in docs/taxonomy.md, which is authoritative. Evidence is train-split only; no dataset rows are stored here.

evidence.cluster_structure: KMeans silhouette ~0 at all k (best 0.0125 at k=10); taxonomy is designed, not discovered
evidence.prevalence_caveat: Ranges bracket two disagreeing proxies: NMF soft-topic shares over-assign, keyword seeds under-assign. Pilot produces real numbers.
evidence.must_caveat: must_proxy_pct is the profile.MUST_PROXY keyword proxy, not a label

values.name: account_access
values.definition: The customer cannot get into, or has lost control of, their account.

values.name: billing_subscription
values.definition: Money has moved, or failed to move, and the customer disputes or questions it.

values.name: plans_eligibility
values.definition: Which plan applies, joining or switching plans, or qualifying for a price, with no specific charge disputed.

values.name: content_availability
values.definition: Content, or the service itself, is absent from the catalogue or the customer's region.

values.name: playback_playlist
values.definition: Music that exists does not play, or playlist/library behaviour is wrong, independent of device.

values.name: app_device_technical
values.definition: The client, or its integration with an OS, device or third-party hardware, malfunctions.

values.name: product_feature_feedback
values.definition: A request for a capability that does not exist, or evaluative feedback on intended behaviour, with nothing to fix.
values.provisional_reason: Narrow seed measures 3.63%, below the 4% viability floor. Seed is demonstrably narrow; pilot must confirm.

values.name: other_unclear
values.definition: Cannot be confidently assigned: too little information, genuinely ambiguous, off-topic or uninterpretable. Also absorbs social-only praise carrying no actionable request.
values.health_metric: Above ~15% in the pilot means the taxonomy is inadequate and must be revised before golden-set labelling.
absorbed: social_praise (removed in 0.2.0 - no valid instance in the 40-item pilot)

attributes.$comment: Orthogonal to intent. Never part of the mutually exclusive intent label.

conversation_state.rationale: DM-followup language predicts a 94.9% reply-DM rate vs 36.7% when absent, but occurs in only 0.41% of openers - far below the 4% class floor. Highly informative as a flag, unlearnable as a class.

urgency.rationale: The pilot's help/need/asap meta-cluster was a register, not a subject; at k=10 it split into two near-identical pleading clusters (DM 56.4% / 45.1%) whose content was account and billing issues.

frustration.rationale: Emotional intensity is an attribute per D9; it never defines an intent.

language.rationale: Observed in 3/40 pilot items (7.5%) - Indonesian, Swedish and Thai - far above the 0.2% character heuristic reported in docs/profile.md, which that document already flags as untrustworthy. Language is a property of the message, not of what the customer wants.
rules: Language is NOT by itself an escalation reason. A non-English message with clear intent is escalated or auto-handled on the same policy as any other.
If a non-English message has sufficiently clear intent, classify the intent normally.
If intent cannot be determined reliably - for language reasons or any other - the intent is other_unclear, and language records why.
'unclear' is for mixed, transliterated or too-short-to-tell cases.

social_nonrequest_indicator.rationale: Politeness co-occurs with real requests constantly, so praise language must be recordable without changing the intent.

rejected.name: help_need_asap
rejected.reason: Urgency register, not a topic. Split into two near-identical clusters at k=10; underlying content was account and billing issues. Represented via the urgency attribute.

rejected.name: explicit_question
rejected.reason: Tested and rejected outright: 41.97% prevalence but reply-DM 34.3% vs 38.8% when absent. No operational signal. Not an intent and not an attribute.

boundary_rules.test: Can the customer get into the account? No -> account_access. Yes, with a disputed charge -> billing_subscription. The token 'account' is not evidence; access failure is.
Has money already moved incorrectly? Yes -> billing_subscription. No -> plans_eligibility.
Does the content exist in the catalogue for this market? No -> content_availability. Yes but won't play -> playback_playlist.

Where would the fix live? Works on one surface and fails on another -> app_device_technical. Fails everywhere, or concerns music logic (shuffle, queue, offline, playlists) -> playback_playlist. Naming a device is not sufficient. Device, OS and app names are context, not evidence: they locate the symptom and never by themselves assign the intent. If no client-specific surface is mentioned, resolve the case under the relevant non-device rule rather than assigning app_device_technical merely from generic wording.

boundary_rules.pair: social/praise vs an actual support request
boundary_rules.test: Is anything actionable present? Any request -> that request's intent with social_nonrequest_indicator=true. Nothing actionable -> other_unclear (social_praise was removed as an intent in 0.2.0; the indicator attribute carries the praise signal).

Does the capability exist? EXISTING capability malfunctioning -> the matching technical intent (app_device_technical for client/OS/device faults, playback_playlist for music logic). Capability DOES NOT EXIST, or the customer is asking for it to be built, added, restored or extended to a new device/platform -> product_feature_feedback. A request for support on a device or OS version that is not yet supported is a request for a capability that does not exist, so it is product_feature_feedback, NOT app_device_technical. Test: 'any idea when you'll update the app to support the iphone x' -> product_feature_feedback. 'your latest update doesn't work on iphone 5 with ios 10.3.3, endless app load screen' -> app_device_technical (it shipped and it is broken).
Plain question about service in a country -> content_availability. Framed as advocacy or campaign -> product_feature_feedback.
other_unclear requires that a careful reader cannot identify the issue, not that it is hard. Multi-issue messages take the issue led with.
Prefer the intent with independent escalation authority: account_access > billing_subscription > other_unclear > all others.

If the customer only names a topic and expresses no request, problem, question or actionable need, the intent is other_unclear. Do NOT infer the issue they probably meant. Example: 'question about billing.' -> other_unclear, not billing_subscription.

If the customer cannot authenticate, is unexpectedly logged out, cannot reset a password, or the account is compromised, classify as account_access regardless of any phone, OS or app context. Device/OS/app mentions describe where the failure occurred, not what failed. app_device_technical applies only when authentication is not the underlying issue.

falsification_criteria: social_praise or product_feature_feedback below 4% in the pilot -> fold in
other_unclear above ~15% -> taxonomy inadequate, revise before golden-set labelling
billing <-> plans confusion above 25% with indistinguishable escalation outcomes -> merge
playback <-> app_device confusion above 25% -> do NOT merge; sharpen BR-4 and re-pilot

coverage_gaps.handling: Classify as other_unclear for now. No creator or artist_distribution intent is being added.
coverage_gaps.evidence: Pilot item P007: a parent asking how to upload their child's music to Spotify. Not content_availability (no existing content requested) and not product_feature_feedback (the capability exists, it is simply not a support channel).
coverage_gaps.revision_trigger: If the pilot surfaces multiple recurring examples of this domain, flag for possible taxonomy revision after the pilot - not during it.

coverage_gaps.handling: Folded into other_unclear in 0.2.0. social_nonrequest_indicator remains an attribute and carries the signal.
coverage_gaps.evidence: The class drew exactly one pilot label (P001, 'love me'), which on review is not praise at all - most likely a song-title request, retrieved because the praise seed matched the bare word 'love'. Zero valid instances in 40 items.
coverage_gaps.revision_trigger: If golden-set labelling shows a recurring pure-praise population needing distinct agent behaviour, reconsider.

coverage_gaps.domain: entitlement-vs-client ambiguity (paid tier, unwanted ads/UI persisting)
coverage_gaps.handling: No new intent. Annotator judgement, recorded as a known ambiguity; label by whichever reading dominates and note it.
coverage_gaps.evidence: Pilot item P006: 'no matter how many times i hit the x it won't go away. i pay for premium... it takes up 1/4 of the screen.' Readable as an app UI defect (app_device_technical) or as an entitlement failure - paying for premium yet still served ads (billing_subscription). No boundary rule separates these.
coverage_gaps.revision_trigger: If the golden set shows a recurring population, add a rule rather than an intent.

changelog.change: Initial 9-intent proposal with 4 attributes and BR-1..BR-9.

Clarification pass before annotation. Added the language attribute; added BR-10 (topic without actionable request); recorded artist/music distribution as an open coverage gap. The 9 intent names and their core boundaries are UNCHANGED.

Post-pilot revision. Removed social_praise (9 intents -> 8); social-only praise folds into other_unclear and social_nonrequest_indicator is retained as an attribute. Added BR-11 (account_access vs app_device_technical). Amended BR-4 (device/OS/app names are context, not evidence). Rewrote BR-5 to point at other_unclear. The remaining 8 intent names and definitions are otherwise unchanged.

Pilot locked. BR-6 clarified: existing-capability malfunction -> technical intent; non-existent or requested capability (including support for a not-yet-supported device/OS) -> product_feature_feedback. Recorded the entitlement-vs-client ambiguity (P006) as an open coverage gap with no new intent. Six approved re-annotations applied to the pilot CSV; intents and attributes otherwise unchanged.
